 Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J. 
1.
Heard Sri Amit Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 70 of 2001, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Bisharatganj, District Bareilly during pendency of the trial.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits, applicant is neighbor of the deceased but in spite of that he has been made accused in the present matter.

4. He further submits, during investigation involvement of the applicant was found false and therefore no charge-sheet was filed against him but during trial he has been summoned under Section 319 Cr.P.C.
5.
He further submits, it appears, with the aid of Section 201 IPC he has also been made accused in the present matter.

6. He further submits, apart from the present case applicant is is having criminal history of one another case but that case relates to Railways Act and in that case applicant has already been acquitted.
He further submits, in the present matter applicant is in jail since 28.10.2025.
7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Considering the argument advanced by learned counsel for applicant and the fact that applicant is neighbor of the deceased and during trial under Section 319 Cr.P.C. he was summoned and criminal history of one case of the applicant has been explained in the instant bail application and in the present matter he is in jail since 28.10.2025, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant - Krishna Pal Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
Krishna Pal Singh vs State Of U.P. on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28866224/

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
(Sameer Jain,J.) January 6, 2026 AK Pandey  Krishna Pal Singh vs State Of U.P. on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28866224/
